title: Employee Record Data Types
module: Module 02: Java Data Types and Type Conversion
objective: Store an integer ID, a short age, and a double salary in suitable Java primitive types and print them.
description:
An organization stores an employee's identification number, age, and monthly salary. Read these three values and store them using suitable Java data types: int for the identification number, short for the age, and double for the salary. Display each value on a separate line in the same order.

Assume the inputs are valid and fit within the selected data types. The salary is less than 10,000,000.
input_format:
Three separate lines:
Line 1: Identification number (int)
Line 2: Age (short)
Line 3: Monthly salary (double)
output_format: Three lines: the identification number, the age, and the salary, in the same order.
hint_1: Use Integer.parseInt(), Short.parseShort(), and Double.parseDouble() to convert each input token.
hint_2: Declare the variables as int, short, and double respectively.
hint_3: Print each variable with System.out.println() on its own line.

title: Bank Account Type Selection
module: Module 02: Java Data Types and Type Conversion
objective: Choose integer types by range and a floating-point type by precision for a real record.
description:
A bank stores the following details for each account:
- account number: a 12-digit whole number
- branch code: a whole number from 1 to 5,000
- account type: a single letter (S for savings, C for current)
- balance: a decimal amount from 0.01 to 9,999,999.99 with at most two decimal places
- active status: true or false

Read these five values in the order listed and store each in the most suitable Java data type. Use the smallest integer type that can hold each whole-number range, and a floating-point type precise enough to keep every balance exactly as written. Display each value on a separate line in the same order.

The balance is written in Java's standard double format (for example, 1500.5 or 1000.0).
input_format:
Five separate lines:
Line 1: Account number (12-digit whole number)
Line 2: Branch code (whole number)
Line 3: Account type (S or C)
Line 4: Balance (decimal number)
Line 5: Active status (true or false)
output_format: Five lines: the account number, branch code, account type, balance, and active status, in the same order.
constraints:
100000000000 <= account number <= 999999999999
1 <= branch code <= 5000
Account type is S or C.
0.01 <= balance <= 9,999,999.99
Active status is exactly true or false (lowercase).
hint_1: Compare each whole-number range with the limits of byte (127), short (32767), int (2147483647), and long.
hint_2: A float keeps only about 7 significant digits, but a balance such as 9876543.21 has 9.
hint_3: Use sc.next().charAt(0) for the account type and Boolean.parseBoolean() for the status.
